description: Axiom-owned out-of-tree proposition sidecar (module+symbol keyed, closed grammar nim-sidecar-expr-v1) for stew/base36.nim decodedLength. Two propositions over the ORIGINAL function body (length == 1 -> result == (length + 4) defect — the law inferred by frozen blind-discovery agent A1, pinned at its suspected input, superseding the first adoption's C_out-pinned instance length == 3 -> result == 2, which is retained as superseded history in the contract doc; length == 2 -> result == 1 control unchanged as the injection guard), adopted with a HASH-BOUND adoption record: the loader recomputes the specification artifact's spec identity (SpecID = H(sorted canonicalSpecIR | origin | ruleVersion)) from the loaded proposition content and fails closed unless it byte-equals adoption.adoptedSpecHash, and verifies adoption.subject.blobSha256 against the actual module bytes at the recorded path under the subject root. The subject tree is READ-ONLY (Zero-Footprint); this file is the only legitimate place the proposition lives.

adoption.basis: adopted verbatim from frozen blind-discovery agent A1 output (see experiments/sidecar-adoption-e2e/FREEZE.md)

subject.source: status-im/nim-stew (stew 0.5.0; byte-identical between the nimble pkgs2 store and the @1853f20b clone)

adoption.provenance: The proposition CONTENT is agent-authored: the defect clause is adopted VERBATIM from frozen blind-discovery agent A1 (zero-context run over the read-only nim-stew clone @1853f20b; the agent independently located stew/base36.nim::decodedLength and inferred result == (length + 4), grounded in stew/base58.nim:55-58 identical docstring 'length + 4', stew/base36.nim:134-138 decode requirement payload.len + 4, tests/test_base36.nim:84-85, with suspected input length = 1 -> returns 0 where the law demands 5); the pinned pre length == 1 is that suspected input — the loader schema requires a non-empty pre (axiom_engine.nim), so the general law carries the minimal grammar-expressible instance pre, and the model binding is deterministic. Content authorship confers NO authority. The AUTHORITY for verifying against it is the explicit adoption act: this committed Axiom-owned sidecar whose adoption record hash-binds the exact proposition content and subject bytes. This record SUPERSEDES the first adoption (defect length == 3 -> result == 2, adoptedSpecHash 8e9564842090127b261c30fdd95db095957ad2628fb5a35e4c4016673441e3be, adopter axiom (followup/sidecar-adoption-binding slice, user-approved mission)) — the superseded proposition and hash are preserved verbatim in docs/spec/nim_stew_base36_sidecar_contract.md (adoption-evolution amendment); they are NOT silently rewritten. Any post-adoption content, ruleVersion, or subject-byte change mechanically invalidates the adoption (loader fail-closed).

semanticCaveats: The typedesc[Base36Types] formal is a static discriminator, not a value parameter: the propositions bind only the declared value param 'length', and the replay renders the call as decodedLength(Base36Types, <length>) (the measured carrier token; the C_out replay shape).

Nim int is pointer-width signed; the proposition clauses use literals (1, 4, 2, 1) far from any overflow boundary, and decodedLength's body ((length * 179) div 277) and the law's length + 4 stay in range on the pinned instances.

The propositions are INSTANCE obligations (pre pins one length per case), not universal theorems: the defect pre length == 1 is the blind agent's suspected input, NOT a claim that the inferred law result == (length + 4) holds or fails elsewhere; SAT on the defect case is a counterexample witness against the adopted law AT that instance, UNSAT on the control case is the injection guard.
nonClaims: NOT a claim that the inferred sizing law result == (length + 4) is correct (or that decodedLength is incorrect) for any input outside the pinned defect instance (length == 1 only); the first adoption's instance (length == 3) remains superseded history, not a co-governing proposition
NOT a claim about encodedLength, decode, or any other base36 symbol
NOT a claim that nim-stew was modified or annotated in-tree (Zero-Footprint)
NOT a claim that the replay validates the sizing formula or the inferred law in general — it observes ONE pinned input per case on the pinned subject bytes

NOT an LLM/mined spec: the proposition content's AUTHORSHIP is a blind agent's output, but specOrigin is pinned soExplicit by explicitSpecFromOverlay and the authority is the hash-bound adoption act; any other declared origin fails closed
